why: Teaches that the true self never began and will never cease to be.
One who stays balanced through pain and pleasure grows steady and free.
What is truly real never ceases; what is passing has no lasting hold.
No sincere effort is wasted, and even a little wisdom guards against great fear.
A focused mind is single; a scattered mind runs in endless directions.
Do your work for its own sake, not for the reward, and do not give up acting.
Work without clinging, staying even in success and failure; that balance is yoga.
When you let go of restless cravings and rest content within, the mind grows stable.
The wise stay untroubled in pain, unexcited by pleasure, free from fear and anger.
Whatever good or bad comes, one who does not cling keeps a well-balanced mind.
Like a tortoise drawing in its limbs, draw your senses back from what pulls at them.
Even a wise person who is trying can be carried away by restless senses.
Dwelling on things breeds attachment, attachment breeds craving, and craving breeds anger.
A disciplined person, free of pull and push among pleasures, comes to peace.
In inner peace sorrows fall away and the mind soon becomes steady.
Senses the mind gives in to drag understanding off course, like a gale driving a ship.
Peace comes to one who stays calm like the ocean as desires flow in, not to one chasing them.
Letting go of cravings, selfishness and ego, one walks on into peace.
Freedom does not come from avoiding work or merely giving things up.
Master your senses with your mind and work without clinging; that is worthy.
Do right action; action is better than inaction.
Do your duty steadily without clinging to results; this leads to the highest.
Great souls reached fulfilment through action; work also for the good of the world.
What a respected person does, others copy; the example we set guides those around us.
Do not let likes and dislikes rule you; they block the path.
Runaway desire and anger are the real enemy within, consuming and polluting all they touch.
Unchecked desire, insatiable as a flame, clouds even a wise person's judgment.
However people come to the Divine, they are welcomed; every path leads there.
Those who came before us worked steadily while seeking freedom; follow their example.
The wise see stillness within action and action within stillness, staying balanced while doing everything.
Letting go of attachment to results, always content, one stays free even while busy.
Content with what comes, free of envy, balanced in success and failure, one is not bound.
Offering wisdom is greater than offering things; all action finds its fulfilment in wisdom.
Learn through humble study, questioning and service; the wise will teach you.
Even the worst wrongdoer can cross beyond every wrong on the raft of wisdom.
Nothing in the world purifies like wisdom, and in time it is found within.
One with faith and self-mastery gains wisdom, and with it soon comes deep peace.
Both letting go and active work lead to the highest good, but selfless action is the better way.
One who neither hates nor craves is easily set free.
Work without clinging and stay untouched, like a lotus leaf on water.
A balanced mind overcomes everything, even here and now.
A steady mind does not soar at good fortune nor sink at bad.
Joy found within, not in outside things, is lasting.
One who is happy within, joyful within and lit from within comes to peace.
The wise, self-controlled and devoted to the welfare of all beings, find peace.
Peace is near to those who know themselves and have calmed desire and passion.
With mind and senses in hand, the wise put away desire, fear and passion and become free.
Knowing God as the Lover of all beings, one comes to peace.
One who is self-controlled and peaceful stays even in heat and cold, pain and pleasure, honour and dishonour.
To the truly wise, a lump of earth, a stone and gold are the same.
Regard lovers, friends and foes, strangers, foreigners and relatives, the righteous and the unrighteous, with an even mind.
Balance matters: not too much eating or fasting, not too much sleep or wakefulness.
Moderation in eating, recreation, work and sleep supports a steady, balanced life.
A calm mind is like a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker.
Little by little, with steady patience, find calm.
Each time the restless mind wanders off, rein it in and bring it back under control.
The harmonised person sees the same Self in all beings and all beings in that Self.
Whoever sees God everywhere is never let go, and never lets go of God.
One who honours God dwelling in all beings lives in God, whatever their way of life.
One who sees others as like oneself, and sees equality in everything pleasant or painful, is a perfect yogi.
The mind is restless, strong and hard to steady, as hard to hold as the wind.
The restless mind is hard to steady, but it can be done through steady practice and letting go.
Inner calm is hard for the undisciplined, but it can be reached by well-directed effort.
One who does good is never destroyed, in this life or the next, and never walks the path of woe.
The suffering, the seeker, the one in need and the wise are all counted among the faithful.
Whatever form a person's sincere faith takes, God makes that faith steady.
God is easily reached by one who keeps God constantly in mind.
Even a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, offered with devotion, is accepted.
Whatever you do, eat or give, do it as an offering to God.
God is the same to all beings; no one is hateful to God, and the devoted live in God.
Even one who has done great wrong, turning to God with a whole heart, is counted righteous.
God speaks to you as one who is beloved, wishing for your good.
Those who share faith, light each other's way and speak of God together are content and joyful.
Whatever is glorious, good, beautiful and strong comes from a spark of the divine splendour.
Arjuna bows before God and asks Him to bear with him as a father with a son, a friend with a friend, a lover with the beloved.
Working for God, free from clinging and without hatred of any being, one comes to God.
If you cannot keep your mind fixed on God, then reach for God by steady practice.
If constant practice is beyond you, devote yourself to God's service; doing your actions for His sake, you will reach perfection.
If even that is beyond your strength, simply let go of clinging to results with a calm mind.
Letting go of the fruits of your work is followed by peace.
Bear no ill-will to any being; be friendly, compassionate, humble, balanced and forgiving.
One who is ever content, self-controlled and resolute, devoted to God, is dear to God.
One whom the world need not shrink from, who does not shrink from the world, free of anxious swings of joy, anger and fear, is dear to God.
Stay the same toward rival and friend, in fame and disgrace, in heat and cold, pleasure and pain.
Humility, sincerity, harmlessness, forgiveness, uprightness, purity, steadiness and self-control mark true wisdom.
The Light of all lights, beyond all darkness, is seated in every heart.
One who sees the same divine presence dwelling equally in all beings truly sees.
Stay balanced in pleasure and pain, value earth and gold alike, and stay steady in blame and praise.
Free of pride and clinging, with desires stilled and beyond pleasure and pain, the wise walk the lasting path.
Fearlessness, a clean life, generosity, self-restraint, study and straightforwardness are marks of a good life.
Harmlessness, truth, freedom from anger, peacefulness, compassion to all, gentleness and modesty are marks of goodness.
A person becomes what they truly believe in; their faith shapes who they are.
Speak words that do not hurt, that are truthful, kind and helpful.
A cheerful mind, balance, quiet, self-control and a pure heart are the discipline of the mind.
A gift given because giving is right, to one who cannot repay, at a fitting time and place, is pure.
Do what ought to be done simply because it should be done, without clinging to the result.
A clear-minded person does not resent unpleasant work nor cling to pleasant work.
No one can give up action entirely; what matters is letting go of the fruits of action.
True knowledge sees one undying being in all beings, undivided among the divided.
Acting rashly, without regard for your strength or the harm and loss to others, is the darkest kind of action.
Work without clinging or ego, with steadiness and confidence, unchanged by success or failure.
Clear understanding knows when to act and when to hold back, what to fear and what not to fear.
Pleasure that is like nectar at first but like poison in the end is called passionate.
Put aside ego, violence, arrogance, craving, anger and greed, and become selfless and peaceful.
Reflect fully on what you have learned, then choose for yourself how to act.
You are beloved and steadfast of heart, and God speaks for your good.
Come to God for shelter; do not grieve, for God will free you from every wrong.
Arjuna says his confusion is gone and his doubts have fled through God's grace; he stands firm and will do as God says.
